fatal_errors: The hypothesis replaces the as-cast equimolar WTaTiVZr versus pure-tungsten comparison with an unspecified tungsten-based alloy subjected to thermal pre-aging.

It attributes behavior to grain-boundary precipitates, whereas the target structural mediator is a segregated two-BCC-phase dendritic microstructure and the proposed strengthening arises mainly from multicomponent solid-solution effects and lattice distortion.
The predicted reduction in plastic strain conflicts with the target advantage, which is increased high-temperature plastic strain and a lower brittle-to-ductile transition temperature.
The proposed testing above 700 °C does not overlap the target temperature range of room temperature to 500 °C or its room-temperature compression and scratch-toughness protocols.

None of the cited evidence directly establishes that increasing coherent grain-boundary precipitate density in a tungsten-based plasma-facing alloy simultaneously suppresses plastic strain and raises fracture toughness.
explanation: The response addresses the broad theme of tungsten-containing fusion materials and offers a nominally controlled aged-versus-unaged experiment, but it does not reconstruct the target material, intervention, baseline, conditions, mechanism, or principal outcome. Its experiment could test whether aging changes mechanical behavior, yet it would not isolate precipitate density unless grain size, segregation, residual stress, and bulk precipitation were independently controlled. The asserted coupling of reduced plasticity with improved toughness is not generally valid; grain-boundary precipitates can instead promote intergranular embrittlement. E2 concerns an FCC/L12 high-entropy superalloy, E3 concerns B2/BCC decomposition and hardness, E4 reports grain-boundary precipitation without the claimed high-temperature toughness mechanism, and E1 provides only general fusion-material context. Thus the hypothesis is neither an exact nor partial reconstruction and lacks direct evidentiary support as a plausible alternative.
